name: Boost.PropertyTree
listed_description: A property tree parser/generator that can be used to parse XML/JSON/INI/Info files. [Boost]
reason: No source claims it is faster than any baseline. Repo page (65 stars, BSL-1.0, last commit 2026-02-06; directories doc, examples, include, test, no benchmark directory) has no performance statement. miloyip/nativejson-benchmark README lists it among libraries that failed integration (number, true, false and null become strings), so it has no rows there. The only numbers found show it losing: facebook/osquery issue 3164 (2017, no hardware or compiler given) has boost::ptree DB_serialize_column_order at 3,493 ns vs RapidJSON 871 ns (4.0x slower), 23,099,589 ns vs 1,388,649 ns at 100/100 (16.6x slower); boostorg/property_tree issue 105 is titled 'read_json takes a long time'. Searches of danielaparker/json_benchmarks, stephenberry/json_performance and mloskot/json_benchmark found no property_tree rows.

name: frozen
listed_description: JSON parser and generator for C/C++.
reason: README and repo page (775 stars, Apache-2.0 now, not the GPL tag in the list; C; last commit 2026-01-05; root has only frozen.c, frozen.h, unit_test.c, Makefile, BUILD) make only the design claim 'Very small footprint' and mention -DJSON_MINIMAL=1; no byte counts, no speed numbers, no baseline named. Not in nativejson-benchmark or any other shootout reached (searched nativejson-benchmark, json_benchmark, schemaless-benchmarks, general web). No benchmark directory, no benchmark issues reachable.

name: JeayeSON
listed_description: A very sane (header only) C++ JSON library.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README (136 stars, BSD-3-Clause, last commit 2017-01-02) mentions no benchmark or speed; the only repo issue matching 'benchmark' is #18 'Conformance report for reference' (miloyip, 2016), a conformance report not timings. nativejson-benchmark ships src/tests/jeayesontest.cpp (guarded by HAS_BOOST and C++14) and lists JeayeSON, but its committed sample performance CSV (Core i7-4980HQ, clang 7.0) has zero JeayeSON rows and the result/ directory holds only scripts. Not in mloskot/json_benchmark either. Web search found no third-party timing of it.
